watchOS 27 will launch this fall as the next major software update for Apple Watch, introducing a practical new feature to extend Apple Watch battery life: "Active Battery Conservation Notifications."

watchOS 27 can proactively extend your Apple Watch's battery life by disabling features you rarely use.

watchOS 27 is just around the corner, bringing two new apps, a practical tap gesture, a brand-new default watch face, three health-related upgrades, and more to Apple Watch.

Another new feature in watchOS 27 aims to extend your Apple Watch battery life.

"Active Battery Conservation Notifications" is a brand-new type of alert that may appear on your Apple Watch.

When you receive a battery conservation notification, it means watchOS 27 has detected features you've never used and disabled them to save battery power.

These features include gesture controls, the "Raise to Speak" function for activating Siri, and the "Start Workout" reminder.

All of these features involve background processing and put a certain drain on battery life.

Therefore, in watchOS 27, if the system detects that you've never used these features, it will automatically disable them. At that point, a "Battery Conservation Notification" will appear to inform you of the arrangement and give you the option to keep them enabled.

If you use these features regularly, you won't receive this notification. Of course, you can also go into Settings at any time to disable them yourself in exchange for longer battery life.

Apple has not specified how much extra battery life disabling these features will provide. However, judging by the fact that the company specifically added this new battery conservation feature, the savings are clearly significant enough to warrant this new design.

Do you usually use features like "Raise to Speak," gesture controls, or the "Start Workout" reminder on your Apple Watch? Will you keep them enabled in the future? Let us know in the comments.
